correctness.rationale: Forth and back give F[N(A)]=N(F(A)). At a singleton source, N(A) is a clique; in the target, the neighborhood of a set of size greater than one contains nonadjacent distinct singletons. Thus atoms go to atoms. N(A) is the union of its atoms' neighborhoods, and target singleton probes recover a world from its neighborhood. This forces direct image on all worlds. Back to the full target world forces the atom map to be onto, and an onto atom map lifts any adjacent target world by choosing representatives including one in the given source world. Counting fibers or inclusion-exclusion gives the displayed formulas; composition and the case n=m follow. This only checks the tiny finite cases.
